title: IMD Issues Yellow Alert for Delhi-NCR as Rain, Hailstorms Forecast
excerpt: Light to moderate rain, thunderstorms and winds of 40-50 kmph hit Delhi on Thursday, October 29, with isolated hailstorms likely in Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh till October 30, while the city's AQI stayed poor at 227.
body:
• The IMD issued a yellow alert for Delhi-NCR on Thursday, October 29, with light to moderate rain, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds, continuing on Friday, October 30.
  • Wind speeds were forecast at 40-50 kmph on Thursday morning, easing to 30-40 kmph for the rest of the day; isolated hailstorms are likely in Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh till October 30.
  • Delhi was expected to reach a maximum of 27 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 17 degrees Celsius on Thursday.
  • Air quality stayed poor despite the rain: the city AQI was 227 at 8 a.m. on Thursday, with Uttam Nagar at 340 in the very poor category.

Moderate rainfall lashed Delhi-NCR on Thursday, October 29, as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a yellow alert forecasting a generally cloudy sky with spells of rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds through the day and into Friday.

The IMD forecast light to moderate rainfall at several places, accompanied by lightning and strong winds. Wind speeds could reach 40-50 kmph during the morning hours, with gusts of 30-40 kmph likely during the remainder of the day, according to the IMD forecast reported by LatestLY.

Hailstorm risk till October 30

The unsettled weather is expected to continue on Friday, October 30, with cloudy conditions and thunderstorms likely to persist over Delhi and neighbouring areas. Isolated hailstorms are also likely in Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh till October 30. News Ei Samay's report gives the same two-day window, October 29 and 30, for the thunderstorm and hailstorm activity over Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi.

Residents have been advised to exercise caution during periods of lightning, hailstorms and strong winds. A yellow alert is the IMD's advisory level signalling that severe weather is possible and that people should stay updated and be prepared, below the more serious orange and red alert levels.

Temperatures dip under cloud cover

The maximum and minimum temperatures in the national capital were expected to settle at 27 degrees Celsius and 17 degrees Celsius respectively on Thursday. The cloudy conditions and rainfall were expected to keep temperatures lower than usual for the period, News Ei Samay reported.

Rain brings no relief to air quality

Delhi's air quality remained in the poor category on Thursday morning despite the rain. The city-level Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 227 at 8 a.m., according to the Central Pollution Control Board's (CPCB) All India AQI portal, with PM2.5 and PM10 identified as the prominent pollutants.

Among monitoring stations, Uttam Nagar recorded an AQI of 340, placing it in the very poor category, followed by Dwarka Sector 8 at 308. Other stations in the poor range included CRRI Mathura Road at 299, Punjabi Bagh at 285, Chandni Chowk at 272, Pusa at 271, NSIT Dwarka at 270, Sirifort at 268, IGI Airport Terminal 3 at 266 and Anand Vihar at 227. Some locations recorded moderate air quality, including Burari at 174, Badarpur at 159 and Chhawla at 154.

Under the CPCB's National AQI classification, readings between 101 and 200 are moderate, 201 to 300 are poor and 301 to 400 are very poor. Prolonged exposure to poor air quality can cause breathing discomfort, while very poor air quality may lead to respiratory illness. The deterioration was already under way before Thursday's rain: the city's AQI stood at 229 on Wednesday, rising from 197 on Tuesday and ending four consecutive days of moderate air quality, according to the CPCB figures reported by News Ei Samay.

What happens next

Cloudy conditions and thunderstorms are likely to persist on Friday as the weather system continues to affect the national capital and neighbouring areas, with the hailstorm risk running till October 30. The combination of rain, thunderstorms and changing winds could bring temporary changes in pollution levels, and residents have been advised to continue monitoring official weather and air-quality updates.
